Ana (CSM): FYI Borealis renewal ~6w. Sudden drop in embedding calls and a new infra lead is running a parallel eval. Procurement asked for a side-by-side cost+latency sheet. Putting triage here.
Ben (AM): drop the usage snapshot?
Ana (CSM): telemetry quick-slice:
30d tokens/day: 35k -> 11k -> 2.9k (last 7d); Active seats: 50 -> 29; Top routes: /embeds 70%, /search 20%, /chat 10%; Errors: none recent; p95 embeddings ~105ms
Clara (Sales): competitor name? what are they promising?
Marcus (Borealis): Procurement looped in "FastVec". They claim ~2x cheaper per-1M embeddings. Finance put new commits on hold pending pilot.
R&D (Eng): we can spin a 7-day dedicated pilot on 2xA10 to reproduce throughput and a caching demo. BYOK/HSM for a full Private deploy needs extra provisioning (+10 business days).
Ben (AM): suggest offer: 7-day pilot (discounted), a short Optimize audit, perf matrix vs FastVec, and a 30-min tech readout. Legal ok?
Clara (Sales): propose 25% pilot discount, Optimize audit free. Tagging Legal. Ana, can you confirm exec sponsor?
Ana (CSM): Exec sponsor is VP Eng (Priya). Marcus, can Priya join a 30-min readout? Also Marcus, what perf targets would satisfy you?
Marcus (Borealis): Priya wants p95 <120ms at our current qps and cost <$28 per 1M embeddings after caching. Also need note on VPC/on-prem feasibility.
R&D (Eng): we'll prepare a perf matrix: cost per 1M (raw), cost per 1M (with KV cache & 8-bit quant), p50/p95 latency at target QPS, and a short reproducible script. For VPC pilot we'll note constraints.
Ben (AM): I'll draft pilot commercial terms and loop Legal. Ana please own scheduling and the finance one-pager.
Ana (CSM): will do. Posting perf checklist to Marcus now. Ops-bot: renewal_watch:borealis:1718865432 created and assigned to @Ana; 72h follow-up reminder set.
Marcus (Borealis): if you can demonstrate >=3x unit-cost improvement with caching+quant within pilot, we can accelerate approval.
Clara (Sales): copying a brief competitive note request to Product for architectural differentiators vs FastVec.
R&D (Eng): quick note for Product: Redwood supports persistent KV/prefix caching + dynamic batching + quantization-aware runtime; competitors often lack persistent KV. We'll include that in the comparative doc.
Ana (CSM): thanks team, I'll post the invite + Marcus's checklist answers here after sync. :thumbsup:
